meta.title: Generic Operator — Generic Kubernetes Operator Engine
meta.description: A generic, Jinja2-template-driven Kubernetes operator engine, with Secure Namespace Operator as reference implementation.

hero.title: Generic Operator
hero.tagline: A generic, Jinja2-template-driven Kubernetes operator engine — with Secure Namespace Operator as reference implementation.

problems.heading: The problem
problems.intro: Building a Kubernetes operator for on-demand provisioning — namespaces, quotas, network isolation, ingress, egress — requires a solid foundation (reconciliation loop, template rendering, revision tracking, RBAC) before writing a single line of business logic.
problems.p1_title: Duplicated code for every new need
problems.p1_text: The kopf loop, template rendering, generic resource application, and revision tracking get rewritten identically from one operator to the next.
problems.p2_text: A homegrown mutating/validating webhook means TLS certificates, cert-manager, and network availability to the API server — operational overhead for what's often simple logic.
problems.p3_text: Without a native OCI registry, publishing and versioning a Helm chart for a platform team stays manual and hard to reproduce.
problems.audience: Target audience: platform / SRE teams operating multi-tenant Kubernetes who need to expose secure, self-service namespace provisioning.

concept.heading: A generic engine, driven by templates
concept.intro: templates/core/ knows the name of no CRD, no spec field, no specific Kubernetes resource. It only follows this pipeline, for whatever CRD you point it at:
concept.step1_text: values.yaml::crd declares group / version / kind / plural. The CRD's OpenAPI schema supplies each field's default value.
concept.step2_text: kopf handlers register on (CRD_GROUP, CRD_VERSION, CRD_PLURAL) read from the environment — never a hardcoded group/kind.
concept.step3_title: It loads the list of templates to process
concept.step3_text: A dedicated ConfigMap lists, in order, which templates to render — configmap/key format, spread across several themed ConfigMaps.
concept.step4_title: Each template is rendered with Jinja2
concept.step4_text: Using the spec values of your CRD instance — custom delimiters so it never collides with the chart's own Helm rendering.
concept.step5_text: Generically, via the Kubernetes dynamic client — whatever apiVersion/kind appears in the rendered YAML, with no fixed Python model.
concept.step6_text: Every spec change bumps a revision annotation and logs a diff into a history ConfigMap.
concept.crd_text: Group, version, kind, plural — one place to change to point the engine at a different CRD, without touching any Python code.
concept.templatecentric_title: Template-centric: Python is just an orchestrator
concept.templatecentric_text: All business logic lives in the Jinja2 templates, not the code. A behavior change is usually a template edit, never an engine change.
concept.order_title: An explicit list of templates to process
concept.order_text: Execution order is declarative — the Namespace before the NetworkPolicy, for instance — and each entry points to a specific ConfigMap and key.
concept.controller_title: Operator + controllers: same engine, continuous mode
concept.controller_text: The operator can spawn a dedicated controller per CRD instance — a separate process that replays the exact same pipeline (steps 3 to 6 above) continuously, to watch external state rather than apply a template once. This mechanism is part of the generic engine, not the implementation.

reference.heading: Secure Namespace Operator
reference.intro: A full implementation of the engine above, shipped with the project — proof the concept works, and a concrete starting point to copy for your own.
reference.w1_text: NetworkPolicies generated automatically, with configurable external-access rules (CIDR, FQDN, services, namespaces).
reference.w2_text: Compute, storage, Kubernetes object counts — bounded per provisioned namespace.
reference.w3_text: NGINX, HAProxy, or Traefik — a dedicated controller per namespace.
reference.w4_text: Automatic VIP placement with L2 announcement and Cilium policies — powered by a dedicated controller, spawned by the operator, one per namespace.
